coverage_notes: All supplied anchors on PDF pp.1-4 were viewed, including complete Table I and metal analyses, Figs.1-6 and anodizing discussion. Rendered labels remained readable despite Poppler font warnings.
shared_qualifications: C7: The paper itself supplies the rounded reference equivalence -0.80 V vs SCE = -0.56 V vs SHE (PDF p.1). Accordingly use E(mV vs SCE) = 1000 E(V vs SHE) - 240 for a source-calibrated comparison at the precision of those rounded values. No target-fitting offset is used. Reference temperature is unstated; 0-40 C are experimental-solution temperatures, not assumed reference-electrode temperatures. The source reports steady-state reproducibility better than +/-15 mV.

All CRA 803-814 targets agree within source/reference rounding and graphical precision, rather than at their excessive decimal precision. obs_004 primary Table I -0.41 V and secondary Fig.1 approximately -0.40 V are both preserved; obs_001 similarly retains text/table -0.40 and plot about -0.405 V.

The paper uses 50 mV potential increments separated by 5 min, followed by at least 12 h holds for steady Vc. CRA Scan Rate 0.167 must not be taken as a continuous sweep rate merely because 50/300 has that numerical value.

CRA 810 solution cell 0.1 M NaCIO4 is preserved verbatim; paper Table I is NaClO4 (perchlorate), not NaCl. Its CRA CL- [M] value 0.1 is inconsistent with chloride species and is not used as evidence of free chloride.

obs_011/CRA 811 retains cited Bond et al. provenance from Table I; source-reported/cited outcomes are not excluded. Fig.5 present corrosion-potential proxies and Kaesche critical-potential points retain their distinct origin/meaning and are not equated to supplied standard steady-state records.

evidence.paper_value: Potentiostatic steps followed by long holds for steady-state Vc
evidence.cra_value: Potentiostatic Polarization. For most of the measurements, Al electrodes were employed measuring 1.5 cm long and 0.4 cm in diameter. One end of each electrode was drilled and tapped, allowing a threaded member attached to a nickel wire to hold the electrode firmly against a glass tube separated by a water-tight Teflon gasket. Only the electrode surface, totally immersed, Teflon, and glass made contact with the electrolyte. Specimens were polished to 3/0 emery paper followed by pickling in 2N NaOH at 80~ for 5 min and then washing in distilled water.
evidence.comparison: Source p.1 distinguishes steady Vc from approximate Vc-prime; no continuous sweep is inferred.
C7: -0.4 x 1000 - 240 = -640.0 mV vs SCE, using paper p.1 rounded equivalence. Compatible within source +/-15 mV reproducibility and/or plot precision; original readings remain unchanged.
